There is no well record within reach at this point, so a site-specific water-table decline rate cannot be assessed. The best available evidence is a regional water-balance proxy from ERA5 reanalysis (via the "anywhere" tool, 10-year window, 2016-08-27 to 2026-08-27, ~9 km grid cell): mean annual precipitation 699.96 mm/yr against reference evapotranspiration 1202.93 mm/yr gives an aridity index of 0.58, classed "dry sub-humid" (UNEP scheme, precipitation/ET0 basis, Allen et al. 1998). This indicates a moisture deficit typical of the region but is not itself a measured groundwater trend.

Based on the Church End Little Hadham groundwater gauge (Environment Agency, station 0f541464-634d-4422-b4a0-c369325108dc, ~4.5 km from your point), the Mann-Kendall trend on annual mean levels over 35 years of usable annual data (within a 57.9-year record spanning 1964-2022) found no statistically significant trend: Sen's slope is +0.0158 m/year, tau = 0.138, p = 0.25. In plain terms, the water table is not detectably falling - if anything the slope is very slightly positive, but this is not distinguishable from noise at conventional confidence levels.
